> I _know_ that that these:
>
>
http://cgi.ebay.co.uk/ws/eBayISAPI.dll?ViewItem&item=3148047836&category=330
55
>
> were legitimatly earned, but a prince selling prize cards doesn't look
> good does it? You could have at least diguised your ebay handle.

If he got them personnaly in a non-prince way, he should have no reason to
disguise himself. But to someone who isn't aware of the way he got the
cards, it sure could look bad.

> This is in no way as bad as TcardsUK selling 5 Lambach's Legion
> tournament kits for £4.95 each- the ramifications of that are just too
> ridiculous to contemplate, but even so.

Now, this IS bad. It also goes toward the number of flaws in the current
prize system. Prize are prize, and shouldn't IMHO be acquired any other way
; or I'm missing something here ! The goal of prize support is to entice
people to come to the tournaments, and therefore promote the game, right ?
Anyone making profit on these without having earned the cards in tournament
is obviously a big problem. As a matter of facts, I even think no one should
be able to order the cards online for a definite price (excluding e-bay or
similar, of course, I'm talking regular distribution here).

Of course, the way things should be handled, or other problems arising from
this, are a discussion for the Conclave list. But the fact you are
mentionning looks like a fatal and obvious flaw of this system to me.

Yours,

Orpheus, Prince of Marseille.

Messages.Author: mgreen02
Messages.Body:
The Lasombra <TheLa...@hotmail.com> wrote in message news:<v134ovge69pbblqfp...@4ax.com>...

> >Which begs the question: why are they being sent these particular
> >boxes of stuff that are not intended for sale?
>
> They were intended for sale, to the stores running events.

Which immediately assumes stores are running events. Which is true for
only one of the six storyline events (Southampton- and that was run
outside the correct timeframe to be considered) held in the UK. The
other events were not run in, sponsered by or had any visable
connection with stores at all.

> Evidently there were distributors that overestimated their areas
> presence in the game.

Or saw a quick profit and sold the kits to whoever for whatever
reason.

> Holding more storyline events was the answer, not criticizing the people in
> it for money (ie, the distributors and stores).
>

The people in it for the money are hindering the situation, not
helping it in this case. Less people are likely to attend of organise
tournaments if they know they can simply BUY the entire prize
structure at a small cost. Not only that, but in this case purchasers
can forego the hassle of actually enticing more people into playing by
buying 10 Lambach's Legion cards and then, THEN, trading those cards
away for a massive profit. All because a distributor can't be trusted
to sell a box to the right person.

To suggest that people need to organise more tournaments to prevent
the kits being sold off is insane.

Matt Green
-at least they didn't ebay them i suppose.

Quite. The storyline in Battle Creek, MI had two, count 'em, TWO whole

Indeed. My experience has convinced me of three things:

Messages.Author: Orpheus
Messages.Body:
> > The people in it for the money are hindering the situation, not
> > helping it in this case.
>
> Quite. The storyline in Battle Creek, MI had two, count 'em, TWO whole
> packs of cards for the prize support in addition to some crappy novels

[first, I don't want the actual argument between Noal and me to turn this
thread into a flame war ; so I'll just state my Pov calmly and expect him to
behave the same ; but I couldn't let the things he said go by unanswered,
even if the troll-bait seems obvious]

So the tournament where you were had some trouble with prize. The 2 packs of
cards (making them 20 of each) and books were standard przie support for
that storyline, for various reasons discussed on Princes list.
The situation lately maybe hasn't been for the best. But some tournies out
there went wonderfully well, including prizewise. No matter : the goal of a
tournament is to have fun, and if the mood was good it should be enough.
Now, if it isn't, maybe the reasons aren't as easy to pinpoint as what you
suggest. Let's have a look...

> > To suggest that people need to organise more tournaments to prevent
> > the kits being sold off is insane.
>
> Indeed. My experience has convinced me of three things:
> 1) Never return to the store in Battle Creek

Some stores do stink. Did the Prince depend on the store (for prize, is it
the only place where they can play, was he able to buy prize with entry fee
at a favoured prize, etc.) ?

> 2) Never, ever be a Prince again so I don't have to put up with the
> total lack of competence on WW's part to handle prize support.

Are you on the Conclave list ? Do you have all the elements to judge of the
inadequacy of WW's handling of Prize Support ? Do you propose any solutions
? Are you aware that despite all the problems, real or imaginary, some
Princes still manage good prize support for every single tournament ?

> 3) Never, ever attend a constructed tournament that I have to pay to
> play in unless it's held at a major convention.

Why ? Because you want more prize ? Do you think these are totally related ?
And are you sure the mood of the tournament will be better in a convention
than in some small events ? In my experience, this isn't always the case.
And you could be surprised of what some "normal" tournaments can manage with
prize even without WW's help. Now, of course, being on good terms with the
local shops can't harm.

> I now know why every one is selling off their collection.

I doubt it. Some very different people have been selling their collections,
and most of them invoked very different reasons. The one I saw more
frequently were : the groupings, the too numerous (or sometimes erratic)
rulings or erratas, the mood of the tournaments, getting ruined by deals...
I saw Princes resigning from their place, sometimes because of inadequacy
between their view and WW's politics, but most of them also said that they
would keep playing, and not sell their collection. So I believe that you're
interpreting some facts (people selling their collections, which happens all
the time in a trading / fashionable game) the way it best seems to suit your
arguments.

> At this
> rate, it won't be long before I join them.

Because you went to a tournie with not enough prize support ?! Well, I'm
sure this is the right spirit.

This isn't the place to discuss eventual trouble between Princes and WW's
organisation : the Conclave is. If you have some trouble with a shop, a
Prince, or whomever was in that tournament, this might be the place. Or not.
But if you don't have all the proper elements you have no ability to judge
who is responsible for what. And if you do have them, it means you're a
Prince, because you love this game and want to help it grow. As this doesn't
seem to be the case, it certainly is easier to criticize (without any proper
arguments) the works of others than to propose interesting solutions (as a
Prince on the Conclave or as a player worried about the game he loves right
here). But I don't believe this leads to anywhere of interest.

---------

Orpheus

Messages.Author: Matthew Heslin
Messages.Body:
"Noal McDonald" <dhar...@my-deja.com> wrote:
> Quite. The storyline in Battle Creek, MI had two, count 'em, TWO whole
> packs of cards for the prize support in addition to some crappy novels
> by WW that nobody wanted. This for a tournament that I had to pay $5
> to participate in.

Noal, I know Battle Creek had some attendance
issues, but did the retailer charge you in relation to the
cost of the prize kit? Or was that $5 a general fee to
play cards in his shop?
In defense of the novels/graphic novels, for a format
specifically designed to play with new blood, I think
they make sense - I offered the novels/graphic novels
to the new players at my tournament as a prize for
being new. They turned them down, so I'll keep offering
them to new players, etc.
In general, I think that the prize kits weren't bad--
these weren't supposed to be high-competition,
big-reward events; the "prize" was the chance to get
a new card for your clan and for your region. The
Legions were the main thing my players were interested
in, and Advanced Lambach didn't hurt either.
Note: I also paid out of pocket for a little stack of
prize support for finalists. I don't expect White Wolf
to cover all bases in all cases.

> Indeed. My experience has convinced me of three things:
> 1) Never return to the store in Battle Creek

I can dig that, based on your description.

> 2) Never, ever be a Prince again so I don't have to put up with the
> total lack of competence on WW's part to handle prize support.

Now, that's a bit extreme. WW does more than
most companies, and recent difficulties can and should
be worked out between Princes and them. Then again,
I haven't experienced any difficulties, personally, so
it may be easy for me to say so...

> 3) Never, ever attend a constructed tournament that I have to pay to
> play in unless it's held at a major convention.

There's your gap in reasoning -- come to Wisconsin!
No charge for playing, prize support is live, we have
leftover Lambachs and Legions as gimmes... plus you
guys owe us for all the Michigan trips we've made. : )

> I now know why every one is selling off their collection. At this
> rate, it won't be long before I join them.

C'mon, Noal. It can't be that bad, can it?

Lately I've been thinking to myself, as I read the
pissy rantings of people who didn't get their stuff and
didn't get it on time and such... and think, "Man, this
game almost died. We didn't have any cards, let alone
any prize support. Things could be a lot worse." I think
this makes me more likely to accept things as they are,
sure, but I figure it gives us perspective. Dunno. That's
just me.

good luck with it all,
heslin

alternative location to play the final in. We ended up in a Burger

Hmm the comics whilst a great idea have been very poorly executed. TBH it's
probably a bit unfair to slam WW themselves about it though, as it's likely
that Moonstone themselves chose the artists and storyboarders. I think my
hamster could draw better than some of the guys they chose. Seeing more
comics *would* be cool, but only if WW could address these problems by
picking a better partner or doing it themselves?

> I *may* get around to reading the novel I won in Toronto, but I'm not
> too eager. I found the original clan novel Tremere by the same author to
> be written competentlly, but completely incomprehensible at the same
> time. I'm told that the trilogy carries on where that one left off. The
> Tremere are not a clan that interest me much thematically. But I can
> never have too many books.

The Clan Novel was bearable. The Clan Trilogy is dog-shite, making very
little sense (and not even attempting to try) over the course of the entire
narrative.

> For the record, other White Wolf novels and short stories have actually
> been very good IMHO.

Well that's being very generous. As someone who has collected *all* the
fiction since day one, it's been all over the place. Editorial decisions
seem to be very inconsistent, but this may be because different people have
been making them each time? Things started well with the Beast Within, Dark
Prince and Prince of the City, but then Robert Weinberg's Red Death trilogy
sucked horribly. The matching trilogies of the Garil Covenant and the Blood
Curse were a little better, but they seriously lost their way towards the
end. The Clan Novels were a seriously mixed bag, with a lot of them hardly
mentioning the clans they were supposed to be about. IMHO the best standing
heads above the rest is Setite, the worst being the Giovanni, but not by
much. And don't get me started on the Tremere trilogy. The best Vampire
novel overall out of all of the releases is the first book of the Hunter
sextet - Predator - this beats every other book hands down for the
consistency, quality and development of the narrative.

From an editorial purist point of view what we keep seeing are incomplete
stories told from too many points of view. There are so many occaisions
where, within the space of a single page you step through the eyes of four
or five characters. In many cases it seems that the author is just going
through the motions necessary to depict an event required by the line
developer. It's pretty sloppy and heavy handed IMHO and I'm very surprised
that the quality control has not been a lot tighter. We also keep getting
shards of different stories that are woefully incomplete or left
unexplained. This is fine for RPG material, but if that's all it is supposed
to be, then why not just put it in a V:TM supplement rather than something
that is supposed to be a 'novel'.

Err, sorry, rant over. Went on a bit of a tangent there. I'd be interested
to see what other people think though - hopefully I'm not alone? :)

Regards,

Mike

> Curse were a little better, but they seriously lost their way towards
the
> end.

I picked up the first of the Grail Covenant and liked it a lot. The
Lasombra clan always seemed pretty cool to me. But I could never find
the second and third novel. I had actually assumed that they were never
made. Haven't read Blood Curse.

> The Clan Novels were a seriously mixed bag, with a lot of them hardly
> mentioning the clans they were supposed to be about. IMHO the best
standing
> heads above the rest is Setite,

Most people say this. I agree. Hesha seems to be the most interesting of
the signature characters.

> the worst being the Giovanni,

A lot of people say this also. I actually liked it a lot. It got away
from the elder-powerful-mega-vampire-character and showed "life" as a
vampire from the POV of a piddly little shit who barely deserved
immortality in the first place (and his clan knew it). I dunno... I
liked how it showed some of the basics of being a vampire. The horror of
losing control to a frenzy. The crap of being trapped in a rigid
hierarchical family and knowing that you will never rise above your
current station. I like that Chas had only barely heard of Necromancy.
The clan didn't see fit to teach him because his role as a thug did not
require it. And his disadvantage on the card version pretty much sums up
his incompetence.

> The best Vampire
> novel overall out of all of the releases is the first book of the
Hunter
> sextet - Predator - this beats every other book hands down for the

Interesting. I'll have to check that one out.

> From an editorial purist point of view what we keep seeing are
incomplete

surprised
> that the quality control has not been a lot tighter. We also keep
getting
> shards of different stories that are woefully incomplete or left
> unexplained.

Even though the clan novels came out over a period of a year and a half
or so... it all seemed very rushed.

Since you are collecting all of the WW fiction, have you started on the
Dark Age clan novels yet? Any good?

Cheers,
WES

> Excuse me sir, but your constant boasting is something so childish i'm just
> wonedering if all i read there is real.
> Personnaly i don't give a damn of the national jyhad league. I don't recall

> them "hey , i was here first" and "i'll never tell you what i know, you
> newbie !". Exactly like you did in kindergarten, probably. What is important
> is what's happening right now. Instead of proposing some answers, you're
> just moaning in the tiring "oh things were so much better yesterday"-style !
> If some errors are not to be repeated, you're the one who should inform us.

I agree completely. Seems like the old and boring ranting about how
the 1st edition of pen-and-paper Vampire is way better than the 2nd
(or the 2nd is way better than the Revised one; you bet 95% of the
"ranters" started playing with the edition they're defending).

I've played Jyhad sometime in 96 or 97 and came back to the game last
year, so even if I'm a newbie to some, I can recall the Jyhad first -
and very confusing - decks and a time where we had no tournaments
because there were no NJL in Brazil (as far as I knew of). Now, we
have web pages dedicated to the game (in Portuguese), almost one
tournament per month, and the local retailer did everything right to
guarantee that our packs have arrived. All three Storylines held in
Sao Paulo (the state) area went pretty well, with all the prize
expected. If some didn't care about the novels is another matter. I
got one in a final and I'm reading it. May not be superb, but it's
entertaining and worth since I've paid around U$ 1,33 as entry fee for
playing - and the most important thing to me was having the
opportunity to test a new deck in a competitive environment (and to
get some Xaviars without spending around U$ 70 to import a booster
display of an expansion I don't want to use for the moment). Making 2
finals in 3 tournaments was good enough. Some of you guys bitch about
the stores, distributors and retailers who are "in it for the money"
and can't spare 2 to 5 bucks to meet people and play in a more
competitive style? How does it cost to you to get into a local gig,
for example? If you were chess players I would understand it, but it's
a cardgame, and I bet you've spent 20 times it *per month* to build
your collection.

Though I was informed by the local prince that we were lucky to get
the packs in time for the tourneys while WW had a lot of problems with
distribution around the world, I still suspect that some people made
the whole thing the harder way. Our princes centralized the prize
orders for all tournaments in the whole country in one shop; when the
shop received the packs, the Princes from Sao Paulo sent them all over
the country by regular mail. Until now, I knew of just one event that
didn't have the expected attends to be held properly. One had no
extended prize since they had around 30 players when it was expected
40 or more, but it was fun, nobody went bitching about the quality of
the novels, and the new players were very happy to gain something as a
consolation prize - they've paid some bucks just to feel what it is to
attend a tournament, even certain that they couldn't stand a chance
against the old-timers. AFAIK, Storyline events are held to attract
new players, and we're getting lots of them lately.

Maybe we're talking about old-fart boredom disguised as "outside
organization problems", but I can speak only for some people I know,
not for foreign ones in a newsgroup debate. And I see people here who
can't, or won't, do anything to attract new players; in fact, they do
everything to maintain their Old Boy's Club, and get very angry when a
"newbie" ousts them in a tourney. So suddenly it all turns to things
like "[put in here any expansion as appropriate] is crap", "WW is all
about the money", "they screwed up with [Thoughts Betrayed/Immortal
Grapple/5th Tradition/whatever zillions of cards as appropriate when
he was ousted]", and so on.

Please, this is a game. It needs new players, it needs new tryouts,
even if it doesn't seem to function that much, it needs to be
profitable to survive. Everything else is just bitching for nothing.
